```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 08_hypothesis_testing_sample_z_score
title: >
  Calculate the z-score for the Sample Mean
questions:
  - id: spider_sample_z
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      A sample of 3 has mean 189. The population mean is 284 and the population
      standard deviation is 50. What is the sample z-score?
    answer: -3.29
    tolerance: 0.01
    explanation: >
      The standard error is 50 / sqrt(3). The z-score is (189 - 284) divided by that
      standard error, about -3.29.

  - id: spider_sample_mean_evidence
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      Why is a sample of three people with a mean of 189 milliseconds more unusual
      than one person with a score of 189 milliseconds?
    options:
      - text: >
          Sample means vary less than individual scores, so 189 falls farther into
          the tail of the sampling distribution.
        correct: true
      - text: >
          The mean of the sampling distribution changes when the sample gets larger.
      - text: >
          Individual scores cannot be converted to z-scores.
      - text: >
          A sample of three eliminates sampling error.
    explanation: >
      The sampling distribution has a smaller standard deviation: the standard
      error. The same difference from 284 therefore produces a more extreme z-score.
```
